title: Unify embeddings/rerank cursor model and retry/error semantics for compatibility shim
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: We have multiple legacy clients calling embeddings and rerank endpoints with slightly different pagination and error behaviors. Some clients expect cursor-based pagination with opaque cursors; others poll for page offsets. Error mappings differ: legacy clients treat 429/5xx differently which causes unexpected retry loops and customer-visible flakiness. Goal: implement a compatibility shim and converged contract that preserves legacy client behavior where necessary while providing a single canonical API for new clients. The shim should map legacy client variants to the unified contract without requiring changes from customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests from legacy keys with header X-Legacy-Client or with historical SDK versions are routed through the compatibility shim. 2) Responses contain: items (list), next_cursor (opaque string or null), page_size (int), total_estimate (optional). 3) Cursor semantics: opaque token encoding: stable-order-anchor + server-timestamp; server guarantees cursor validity for 24 hours. 4) Error mapping: canonical 400 for bad cursor, 401/403 preserved, 429 returned with Retry-After header (seconds); transient 5xx normalized to 502 with standardized retry_hint in body for legacy clients that don't parse Retry-After. 5) Backwards compat: legacy clients that expect offset-based pages receive identical item ordering and page boundaries as before. 6) Contract tests and interop test matrix pass for 5 sample legacy SDK versions.
api_spec_notes:
- Response envelope (canonical): {
  "items": [embedding objects],
  "next_cursor": "opaque-token" | null,
  "page_size": integer,
  "cursor_debug": optional string for internal ops (only returned when X-Debug-Cursors=true)
}
- Cursor token contains: base64({"anchor": <sha256 of last-id+sort-key>, "ts": epoch_seconds})
- Pagination semantics: stable server side ordering by score desc then id asc to avoid duplicates across pages. Page_size respected as max items per page. If results change between pages (new documents added), cursor preserves anchor snapshot semantics for consistent traversal until expiry.
- Error mapping table (behavioral, not exhaustive):
  - INVALID_CURSOR -> 400, body {code: "INVALID_CURSOR", message: ...} 
  - CURSOR_EXPIRED -> 410, include suggestion to re-run initial query
  - RATE_LIMIT -> 429 with Retry-After header (seconds) and body {retry_hint: seconds} for shim clients
  - AUTH_FAILURE -> 401/403 as appropriate
  - TRANSIENT_INFERENCE_FAILURE (GPU OOM / kernel crash) -> 502 with retry_hint; increment metric compat.shim.transient_502
- Legacy offset emulation: shim must map offset=N + limit=M into cursor-based traversal deterministically for requested range; performance caveat: large offsets will be throttled with explicit guidance in response.
design_decisions:
- Use a lightweight compatibility proxy at the API edge to avoid touching downstream runtime logic. The proxy will: detect legacy client signatures, rewrite request to canonical cursor query, and materialize responses in legacy shape when requested.
- Keep cursor token structure opaque to clients; provide optional cursor_debug for Red team and debugging only.
- Cursor expiry: 24 hours to balance state storage vs. customer recovery. Shorter TTL leads to more 410s, longer TTL increases storage indexing complexity.
- Error normalization: prefer explicit 429 with Retry-After over silent 5xx for rate signals. For compatibility, include retry_hint in JSON for clients that only parse body errors.
- Rollout via feature flag 'compat-shim-emb-rerank' per-api-key and per-region; start in us-west-2 canary group.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of traffic from legacy-sdk-1.x keys to shim in us-west-2. Monitor errors, latency, and diff in item ordering. Phase 2 (broader): expand to 25% and run contract interop tests with top customers. Phase 3: default enable for all legacy keys while keeping opt-out flag for customers. Phase 4: deprecate legacy offsets in docs after 90 days of stable rollout. Provide customer migration playbook with sample SDK patches and curl examples.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: cursor encode/decode, expiry, invalid tokens.
- Contract tests: golden responses for 6 historical SDKs.
- Integration tests: end-to-end through proxy -> runtime using synthetic dataset with stable ordering.
- Load tests: simulate high-volume small-page pagination patterns to validate latency and steady-state memory.
- Chaos tests: simulate downstream 5xx and GPU restarts to validate error normalization and retry signals.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: cursor expiry causes customer-visible 410s shortly after rollout. Mitigation: conservative TTL (24h) and clear message with re-run guidance; temporary whitelist for critical customers.
Risk: shim adds latency to non-legacy traffic. Mitigation: route only legacy-flagged traffic through shim and benchmark proxy p95 < 10ms added.
Risk: mismatch between offset emulation and historical SDK ordering. Mitigation: create record-level stable sort and snapshot tests; add a fallback mode that returns exact legacy pages by materializing result set for small queries.
monitoring_and_slos:
- Metrics: compat.shim.requests, compat.shim.errors, compat.shim.latency_p50/p95/p99, compat.shim.cursor_expiry_rate.
- Dashboards: per-region error breakdown, legacy-key churn, diff-rate of item ordering vs baseline.
- SLOs: compatibility shim p95 added latency < 15ms; error rate increase <= 0.5% for affected keys. Auto-rollback threshold: >1.5% customer-impacting errors over a 30m window.
rollout_steps: 1) Feature flag deploy to edge proxies (canary). 2) Enable logging and cursor_debug sampling 1% for first 48h. 3) Run canary for 72h; validate contract tests and customer feedback. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% for legacy keys over 2 weeks. 5) Announce deprecation timeline and publish migration guide.

updates: 2025-02-11: Initial spec drafted and shared with ENG/UX. Key open items: cursor format, TTL, and offset-emulation cost model.
2025-02-12: Engineering review (ENG-48210): recommended moving offset emulation to an async path for offsets > 10k to avoid head-of-line latency. Added to dependencies.
2025-02-13: Design review: suggested optional cursor_debug field gated behind X-Debug-Cursors header to avoid leaking internal tokens. UX requested example responses for docs.
2025-02-15: Security review queue: confirmed no new PII will be stored in cursor token; tokens will be HMAC-signed. Security review required=false.
2025-02-18: PM sign-off on acceptance criteria. ENG estimate confirmed at 5 and ENG owner assigned. Canary planned for 2025-02-22 in us-west-2.
2025-02-18: Links to draft design doc and initial PR added to attachments and links.
